summary:
Public-web user icon now opens an AuthModal (LOCAL phone/password login + register, Google OAuth only — Facebook is deliberately deferred/disabled on the public surface per task.md §11) when signed out and an anchored AccountPopover (Đăng xuất) when signed in, on both desktop header and mobile bottom nav via a single shared UserMenuTrigger. Backend: RegisterDto/RegisterUseCase/CreateAccountUseCase accept and persist an optional address (no migration needed); GoogleOAuthClient + OAuthLoginUseCase + OAuthController implement the full authorization-code flow for Google. FacebookOAuthClient exists as deferred, DI-registered-but-unwired code (task.md explicitly allows keeping unactivated code for a future rollout) — OAuthController.parseSocialProvider excludes `facebook` outright and identity-access.module.ts no longer includes it in the active OAuthClientRegistry, so /auth/oauth/facebook/* fails closed before any provider contact regardless of env/DI state. Fixed a pre-existing AuthProvider.isAuthenticated bug that would have made the whole feature appear permanently signed-out. Ten review cycles of fix passes since (full per-finding detail in `decisions`): cycle 3 (7 findings) moved OAuth secrets out of URLs, validated OAuth payloads at runtime, fixed a forgeable oauth=success param, made self-registration atomic, handled unconfigured providers gracefully; cycle 4 (7 findings) hardened the OAuth-race and registration-rollback e2e tests with real concurrency/table-count proof, added a configured-Facebook e2e path, logout-failure and duplicate-submit UI tests, and fixed an e2e port-flake; cycle 6 (5 findings) made the Facebook Graph API version config-driven (v19.0 was retired), made first-time OAuth provisioning atomic with session issuance, fixed refresh rotation mislabeling social sessions as LOCAL, regenerated a complete provenance manifest, and fixed a real Dialog focus-trap bug; cycle 9 (4 findings) fixed a Dialog panel-positioning bug (DialogClose rendered against the viewport instead of the panel), regenerated stale runtime provenance/summary/database-invariants artifacts, built a Facebook OAuth v26.0 contract harness anchored to Meta's official docs (no real credentials available for a live sandbox) which also surfaced and fixed a malformed-state-cookie 500 bug, and captured new real-browser evidence for the signed-in popover and mobile registration; cycle 10 (3 major findings + 1 missing-evidence item) fixed a real credential-leak bug (OAuth authorization codes/state were still fully readable via `req.url` in every centralized log line despite `req.query` redaction), replaced the self-referential Facebook contract test with one bound to a hash-verified pinned-commit snapshot of Meta's own official open-source Graph API SDK (developers.facebook.com/graph.facebook.com are confirmed DNS-blocked from this sandbox, so GitHub was used instead), fixed the standalone `/login` route which still posted the legacy `{email,password}` shape the backend has never accepted, and added a negative test for a provider error paired with a missing/mismatched state; cycle 13 (2 major findings) resolved a review-cycle-9/10/11 loop that kept re-verifying an unverifiable Facebook transport contract by instead applying task.md's own explicit, always-effective requirement — Facebook must be fully disabled on the public surface, not merely 'best-effort contract-verified' — so `OAuthController.parseSocialProvider` now excludes `facebook` outright (fails closed before any provider contact or `OAuthClientRegistry` resolution, regardless of env/DI state) and `identity-access.module.ts` no longer includes `FacebookOAuthClient` in the active `OAuthClientRegistry`; the self-contradictory contract spec (its own pinned fixture documented GET while the spec asserted POST) and its fixtures were deleted, replaced by e2e tests proving the public Facebook routes fail closed even with a fully working client DI-overridden in; separately, fixed a real focus-management bug in `AuthModal` where switching login<->register unmounted the focused view-switch button and dropped `document.activeElement` to `<body>`, letting a forward Tab escape the dialog — fixed by focusing the (now ref-forwarding) `DialogTitle`, which persists across the view swap, from the switch handlers; verified via new jsdom tests and real-browser (Playwright) evidence at desktop+mobile. Cycle 15 (2 major findings) fixed a real OAuth CSRF/state-bypass bug — OAuthController.callback checked providerError before validating state/cookieState, so a forged cross-site ?error=access_denied callback with missing/mismatched state was accepted as a clean denial and consumed the victim's state cookie; reordered so state is validated before any callback outcome (success or provider-reported error) is trusted, with a new regression test proving a forged denial cannot be accepted; and recaptured desktop/mobile browser evidence as one current-cycle, provenance-bound Playwright capture (browser-review-015, 24/24 assertions true) that supersedes browser-review-009/013 and is now bound into a regenerated provenance manifest (61 inputs, 19 artifacts). Review-cycle-16 fix pass (fix-request-review-016.md, 3 major findings, full-plan scope): #1 OAuthController.callback now only consumes (reads-and-clears) the state cookie once the callback is proven to belong to the current attempt (provider supported AND state exactly matches the cookie) — closing a SameSite=Lax forged-callback bug where an invalid/mismatched/unsupported callback could evict a different, still-valid in-flight attempt's state cookie out from under it; proven with a real request.agent(...) browser-like cookie jar (built against an explicit http://localhost:<port> base URL, working around supertest's server-object form always targeting 127.0.0.1, which never matches this app's Domain=localhost cookies under real cookie-jar domain matching — see the new knowledge_updates entry). #2 added current-cycle HTTP e2e coverage for Google's provider_unavailable redirect (DI-overridden unconfigured GoogleOAuthClient exercised through the real /auth/oauth/google/start route) plus 3 new frontend oauth-redirect-handler tests (provider_unavailable message mapping, unmapped-reason generic fallback, unrecognized-oauth-status boundary case). #3 provenance.json now records per-repo source_state (HEAD, base_ref, dirty-inventory sha256 fingerprint) and binds the identity-access/user-profiles schema migrations plus the roles/permissions seed use-case as e2e/transaction dependencies (64 inputs, up from 61; 19 artifacts unchanged, all refreshed). Backend unit 310/310, e2e 142/142 (was 140/140); frontend public-web 107/107 (was 104/104), ui 37/37; full validate-code --tier full green for both repos (run twice — once before, once after fixing the new e2e test's cookie-jar/localhost-port issue found during self-review); all workspace-level deterministic checks (check_handoff, check_provenance x2, sync_provenance, build_evidence_matrix, execution-plan validation) PASSED.

Attempt 56 (review cycle 17, fix-request-review-017.md, 2 major findings, full-plan scope, sensitive auth/security correction): #1 fixed — implemented the previously-missing half of task.md §11's 'kiểm tra state/nonce' requirement: GoogleOAuthClient now requests and fully verifies a real OIDC ID token (RS256 signature against Google's live JWKS via Node's built-in crypto, trusted issuer, audience, expiry, and a nonce minted alongside state and bound 1:1 to this exact login attempt through the same state cookie) before trusting any provider identity or issuing a session — no new dependency added. #2 fixed — OAuthController.callback now allowlists only access_denied as user cancellation; every other provider error maps to a stable, safe provider_error reason instead of being misreported as cancellation, and oauth-redirect-handler.tsx now only ever acts on the literal success/error statuses (an unrecognized oauth= value is ignored, never treated as an implicit success). Backend unit 325/325 (was 310/310), e2e 148/148 (was 142/142); frontend public-web 108/108 (was 107/107). Full validate-code --tier full green for both repos plus a real npm run test:e2e run against the shared local-dev stack; all workspace-level deterministic checks (check_handoff, check_provenance, sync_provenance, check_auth_invariants, check_port_bindings, check_module_wiring, check_openapi_contract, check_frontend_security, build_evidence_matrix, execution-plan validation) PASSED — the only non-passing deterministic check remains check_design_system_usage.py's pre-existing, unrelated, already-waived #efe2cf finding. ADDENDUM (2026-08-18, out-of-band user-directed scope change, see decisions[-1]): Google OAuth is no longer exposed on the public surface either — it is now deferred/disabled using the identical mechanism as Facebook (parseSocialProvider rejects every provider; OAUTH_CLIENTS is empty; the only frontend entry point, social-login-buttons.tsx, was deleted). task.md's AC3 was rewritten to match. Facebook's status is unchanged.

decisions.decision: Added AuthContextValue.loginWithPhone/registerLocal as new methods instead of changing login(email, password)'s signature.
decisions.reason: apps/admin-web's login page also calls useAuth().login(values.email, values.password) and is explicitly out of scope (task.md: 'Không thay đổi luồng đăng nhập ... của admin website'). Changing login's signature would have forced a compile-breaking or behavior-changing edit to admin-web to keep it building.

decisions.decision: Fixed AuthProvider.isAuthenticated to derive from access-token presence alone (Boolean(accessToken)) instead of Boolean(accessToken) && Boolean(user).
decisions.reason: Neither the real POST /auth/login, /auth/register nor /auth/refresh response contains a `user` field (only accessToken/portal/sessionId/roles/permissions) — `user` was always undefined for any real backend call, so isAuthenticated was permanently false regardless of a successful login. This is a pre-existing bug that would have made AC #1/#7/#8 (icon switches to account popup once signed in) impossible to satisfy, so it had to be fixed as part of 'cập nhật AuthProvider ... liên quan'.

decisions.decision: OAuth account linking matches strictly on (provider, providerSubject); a social login's email is never used to auto-link to an existing LOCAL or other-provider account.
decisions.reason: Provider-supplied email is not independently re-verified by this backend and using it as a cross-provider join key would let an attacker who controls/spoofs an email at one provider take over an account created under a different provider or LOCAL. Matches task.md's 'quy tắc không trùng danh tính' as a provider+subject uniqueness rule, enforced by the pre-existing DB partial unique index.

decisions.decision: No new database migration — RegisterUseCase/CreateAccountUseCase already accepted `address` end-to-end (only RegisterDto/register.use-case.ts input types were missing it), and the OAuth (provider, provider_subject) uniqueness needed for find-or-create/race-safety was already a partial unique index from migration 1786791535416-CreateIdentityAccessSchema.
decisions.reason: $create-backend-migration only applies when schema actually changes; verified via source reading and a real migration:run/migration:show against an isolated Postgres that no pending migration exists.

decisions.decision: OAuth start/callback (GET /auth/oauth/:provider/start, /callback) are full-page browser redirects, marked @ApiExcludeEndpoint() and intentionally absent from openapi-contracts.json.
decisions.reason: They have no JSON request/response DTO (redirect Location header only) and are never called through the generated API client — SocialLoginButtons navigates via window.location.href. Covered by apps/api/test/oauth-flow.e2e-spec.ts instead of a Swagger contract test.

decisions.decision: CSRF/replay protection for the OAuth flow uses a short-lived HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax state cookie compared against the `state` query param, cleared on every callback regardless of outcome.
decisions.reason: The callback is reached via a top-level GET navigation from accounts.google.com/facebook.com — SameSite=Strict would drop the cookie; Lax is the correct/minimum setting that still blocks CSRF via non-navigational requests. Clearing unconditionally makes a replayed callback URL fail (missing cookie) even if the authorization code were still somehow valid.

decisions.decision: A concurrent/replayed OAuth callback for a brand-new identity that races on the DB's (provider, provider_subject) unique index self-heals: OAuthLoginUseCase catches the translated provider_identity_already_exists conflict and re-resolves the winner's identity to issue a session, instead of surfacing an error.
decisions.reason: Mirrors the existing phone_already_exists handling pattern for registration races (fix-request-review-3 #1) and matches task.md's 'callback lặp' edge case requirement — a double-submitted callback should behave like a normal repeat login, not a hard failure.

decisions.decision: Ran the backend e2e suite against a fully isolated, uniquely-named Postgres/Redis/MinIO stack (containers m5-pg/m5-redis/m5-minio on scratch ports) instead of the shared `docker compose --profile infrastructure` project.
decisions.reason: The pre-existing 'memories-backend' container set on this host (26h+ uptime) was not publishing its Postgres port as its own compose file specifies, and host port 5432 was answered by an unrelated container with different credentials — consistent with another concurrent task session using the same fixed compose project name. Recreating those shared containers to fix the port mapping risked disrupting that session, so an additive, fully isolated stack was used instead; it was torn down after evidence capture.

decisions.decision: The existing standalone apps/public-web/app/(auth)/login and /(auth)/register pages were left unchanged and simply unlinked from the header/bottom-nav, rather than deleted or redirected.
decisions.reason: task.md's scope is the icon-triggered modal experience; removing/redirecting the standalone routes was not required by any acceptance criterion and risked unrelated regressions (e.g. any deep link or crawler hitting /login). Out-of-scope guard: 'Không mở rộng scope nếu chưa có trong task/addendum.'

decisions.decision: fix-request-review-3 #1: FacebookOAuthClient.exchangeCodeForProfile now exchanges the code via a POST body (client_id/client_secret/redirect_uri/code as form fields, same shape as GoogleOAuthClient) and fetches the profile with the access token in an `Authorization: Bearer` header instead of query-string params.
decisions.reason: The Facebook Graph token/userinfo endpoints previously carried client_secret and the provider access token as URL query parameters, which get logged by URL-oriented proxies/telemetry/error handlers — a credential-leak risk task.md prohibits. Facebook's OAuth endpoints accept both forms; POST body + Authorization header keep secrets out of any URL exactly like the existing GoogleOAuthClient.

decisions.decision: fix-request-review-3 #5: both OAuthClients now validate the token/profile HTTP response bodies at runtime (via a shared assertOAuthResponseField helper in oauth-client.port.ts) and throw DomainError.externalDependency if access_token or the provider subject (sub/id) is missing or blank, before ever returning an OAuthProfile.
decisions.reason: A 2xx response is not a trusted contract — a provider bug or compromised proxy returning `{}` would previously have flowed an empty providerSubject into AuthIdentity.create/persistence, since only LOCAL identities validated providerSubject and the ORM column is nullable. Failing closed here means OAuthLoginUseCase never receives a profile it could use to create a broken account.

decisions.decision: fix-request-review-3 #2: OAuthRedirectHandler no longer reports oauth=success from the URL alone — it now reads useAuth().isAuthenticated/isLoading (rendered inside AuthProvider) and only surfaces the success toast once AuthProvider's refresh-on-mount call has settled and actually authenticated the session; a forged ?oauth=success with no real session now surfaces the same failure toast as oauth_failed.
decisions.reason: The oauth query param is attacker-controlled (a bare `/?oauth=success` link needs no server round trip); trusting it directly would let a user be shown a false 'signed in' state. Waiting on AuthProvider's own refresh call ties the notification to the actual, cookie-verified session outcome.

decisions.decision: fix-request-review-3 #3: RegisterUseCase now opens a single owning `unitOfWork.withTransaction` around the entire flow (CreateAccountUseCase call + permission check + token/session issuance + RefreshSession.save); TypeOrmUnitOfWork.withTransaction was made reentrant (joins an already-active transaction via TypeOrmQueryRunnerContext instead of opening a second, independent connection/transaction).
decisions.reason: CreateAccountUseCase already opens and commits its own transaction, so RegisterUseCase's separate, later transaction for session issuance meant a session-stage failure (e.g. token signing, refresh-session persistence) left a fully committed Account/AuthIdentity/AccountRole/UserProfile behind with no way to register that phone again — violating AC6's 'trong 1 giao dịch nhất quán'. Making the unit-of-work reentrant is the minimal, generic fix: every other repository already resolves its query runner through the same TypeOrmQueryRunnerContext (AsyncLocalStorage), so nested use cases transparently participate in the outer transaction with no change to their own code.

decisions.decision: fix-request-review-3 #7: OAuthController.start now catches both an unrecognized provider name and a resolve()/buildAuthorizationUrl() failure (provider not configured) and redirects to webRedirectUrl with oauth=error&reason=unsupported_provider or reason=provider_unavailable, instead of throwing a raw 400. Extracted the existing callback-only redirectWithError closure into a shared private method used by both start and callback.
decisions.reason: SocialLoginButtons always renders both Google/Facebook buttons regardless of server-side configuration; without this, clicking a button for an unconfigured provider navigated the whole browser away from public-web to a raw backend 400 JSON response instead of a handled, understandable outcome.

decisions.decision: fix-request-review-3 #6: the OAuth provider_subject race e2e test now fires two callback requests through a real Promise.all with a synchronization barrier inside the mocked exchangeCodeForProfile (releases once both requests are in flight), instead of two sequential completeCallback() calls.
decisions.reason: The previous test called completeCallback() twice sequentially, so the second request always observed the first's already-committed identity and never exercised the real provider_subject unique-constraint conflict/recovery path in OAuthLoginUseCase.resolveOrCreateAccountId / TypeOrmAuthIdentityRepository.translateUniqueViolation, despite database-invariants.json claiming real-Postgres race coverage.

decisions.decision: fix-request-review-3 #4: regenerated packages/api-client/src/generated/schema.d.ts from a freshly exported backend openapi.json (npm run export:openapi against the isolated e2e Postgres) and ran it through prettier to match the repo's existing 2-space/single-quote style (openapi-typescript 7.13.0's default output uses 4-space/double-quote, which would otherwise have produced a ~2800-line unrelated formatting diff).
decisions.reason: RegisterDto gained `address?: string` on the backend (task requirement #5) but the committed generated contract had drifted and only exposed phone/password/fullName/email, so typed API consumers couldn't represent the request the raw ApiClient call already supported. Reviewing the post-prettier delta shows only the new address field plus pre-existing @description text drift from unrelated backend Swagger-decorator edits — no manual schema.d.ts edits were made, per the skill's own guidance to run the generation workflow rather than hand-edit the file.

decisions.decision: review-cycle-4 #1: the OAuth-race e2e test now gates on a second, precise barrier — a jest.spyOn wrapping the real AuthIdentityRepository.findByProviderAndSubject that only holds when the call returns null (i.e. the pre-insert preflight lookup) — released only once both concurrent callbacks' preflight lookups have completed, in addition to the pre-existing coarse barrier inside the mocked exchangeCodeForProfile.
decisions.reason: The coarse exchangeCodeForProfile-only barrier proved both requests entered the use case together but not that both reached the actual conflicting INSERT before either committed — one request could still race ahead through its own SELECT+INSERT round trip before the other's SELECT ran, making the provider_subject unique-constraint conflict/recovery path nondeterministic (review cycle 4 finding #1, a regression of review-cycle-3 finding #6). Gating on the null-returning preflight call specifically (not the later winner-lookup call, which returns non-null) avoids deadlocking the resolveOrCreateAccountId catch-and-recover path.

decisions.decision: review-cycle-4 #1: after the race completes, the test now asserts exact row-count deltas (identity.accounts +1, identity.account_roles +1, profile.user_profiles +1, and identity.auth_identities matching this providerSubject == 1) via raw DataSource.query table counts captured before and after the race, instead of only inferring 'exactly one graph' from both responses resolving to the same accountId.
decisions.reason: Same-accountId-on-both-responses proves the two requests ended up pointing at one account but does not, by itself, rule out an orphaned Account/AccountRole/UserProfile row left behind by the loser's rolled-back-but-partially-observed transaction — direct table counts are the only way to prove no orphan row survived, as the review explicitly asked for ('query every affected table').

decisions.decision: review-cycle-4 #2: the registration-rollback e2e test now captures a five-table row-count baseline (identity.accounts, identity.auth_identities, identity.account_roles, identity.refresh_sessions, profile.user_profiles) immediately before the forced session-stage failure and asserts the exact same counts immediately after, in addition to the pre-existing same-phone-retry assertion.
decisions.reason: The prior test only re-registered the same phone and checked the new account had exactly one identity — that proves the failed attempt's LOCAL identity didn't block a retry, but not that every table stayed clean; an orphan Account, UserProfile, AccountRole, or RefreshSession row keyed some other way would have gone undetected (review cycle 4 finding #2, direct proof requested).

decisions.decision: review-cycle-4 #3: added a second, independent e2e app instance in oauth-flow.e2e-spec.ts (own TestingModule/AppModule bootstrap) that overrides FacebookOAuthClient with a controllable fake and GoogleOAuthClient with an 'unavailable' fake — the mirror image of the main suite's setup — and exercises a full configured Facebook start/callback/refresh round trip through the real HTTP/DI/session graph.

decisions.decision: review-cycle-6 #2: OAuthLoginUseCase now provisions a brand-new social account and issues its session inside one owning transaction (`provisionAndIssueSession`), instead of `createAccountForProfile` committing its own transaction before a separate, later transaction issued the token/RefreshSession.
decisions.reason: A permission-check or token/session-issuance failure after the account graph was written used to leave a fully committed Account/AuthIdentity/AccountRole/UserProfile with no session and no way to retry cleanly (review cycle 6 finding #2). `provisionAndIssueSession` wraps `createAccountForProfile` + `issueSessionForAccount` in one `unitOfWork.withTransaction`; on a provider-subject unique-constraint conflict (the concurrent-callback race), that transaction has already rolled back in full by the time the catch block runs (`TypeOrmUnitOfWork.withTransaction` calls `rollbackTransaction()` before rethrowing), so the winner lookup and its session issuance run with no ambient transaction and `issueSessionForAccount` opens a fresh, separate one — race recovery is unaffected. Added a real-Postgres e2e test (`oauth-flow.e2e-spec.ts` 'rolls back the entire first-time account graph...') that forces `issueRefreshToken` to fail after the graph is written and asserts accounts/account_roles/user_profiles/refresh_sessions/matching-identities counts are byte-for-byte unchanged, then proves a retry provisions cleanly.

decisions.decision: review-cycle-6 #3: RefreshSessionUseCase now reads the current RefreshSession's `authProvider` (validated against the `AuthProvider` enum) and reuses it for both the rotated access-token claim and the new RefreshSession row, instead of hard-coding `AuthProvider.Local`.
decisions.reason: Every browser rehydration of a Google/Facebook session (both the OAuth callback's own `/auth/refresh` round trip and any later token refresh) went through this hard-coded LOCAL path, mislabeling social sessions in the access-token claim and the persisted session row — a real, visible correctness bug, not just cosmetic, since anything gating on `authProvider` downstream would misclassify these sessions. Added `apps/api/test/oauth-flow.e2e-spec.ts` assertions (Google + Facebook, including a second chained refresh to prove it survives more than one rotation) and an `apps/api/test/auth-flow.e2e-spec.ts` LOCAL regression test.

decisions.decision: review-cycle-10 #1: `libs/platform/observability/src/logger.module.ts` now installs a custom pino-http `serializers.req` (`redactSensitiveQueryParams`) that redacts `code`/`state`/`access_token`/`token`/`id_token`/`client_secret` from both the serialized `req.query` object and the raw `req.url` query string (split/rebuilt via `URLSearchParams`), instead of relying on pino's `redact: {paths}` option alone.

decisions.decision: review-cycle-13 #2: `AuthModal` now holds a `ref` on `DialogTitle` (made ref-forwarding via `React.forwardRef` in `packages/ui/src/components/dialog.tsx`) with `tabIndex={-1}`, and calls `titleRef.current?.focus()` from the `switchToRegister`/`switchToLogin` handlers right after `setView(...)`.
decisions.reason: Switching login<->register unmounted the previously focused 'Đăng ký'/'Đăng nhập' switch button along with its old view; `Dialog` stayed open so `useDismissableLayer`'s initial-focus effect (deps `[open, onDismiss]`) never re-ran, and the browser dropped `document.activeElement` to `<body>`. From `<body>`, the Tab-trap keydown handler's forward-Tab boundary check (`activeIndex === items.length - 1`) never matched (`indexOf(body)` is `-1`), so it never called `preventDefault()` and a real forward Tab could escape the dialog to background page content — exactly the review's reported bug. `DialogTitle` renders at the same JSX position in both views (only its text content differs), so its DOM node persists across the swap and is always a safe, in-dialog, `tabIndex={-1}` focus target (matching the existing container-fallback convention `useDismissableLayer` already uses when there are no focusables). Verified with new jsdom tests in `apps/public-web/test/auth-modal.spec.tsx` (active-focus-inside-dialog and forward/reverse-Tab-containment assertions after each transition direction) and real headless-Chromium evidence at 1280×800/390×844 (`ai/tasks/MEMORIES-0005/evidence/browser-review-013/`) proving `document.activeElement` lands on the title after each swap, forward Tab lands on the next in-dialog field, and Shift+Tab wraps within the dialog rather than escaping.

decisions.decision: review-cycle-15 #1: OAuthController.callback (libs/modules/identity-access/src/presentation/http/oauth.controller.ts) now validates state/cookieState (present and exactly equal) before checking providerError, and before checking code. Only once state is proven to belong to this browser's own in-flight attempt does the handler branch to access_denied (provider-reported denial) or proceed to exchangeCodeForProfile. Any missing, malformed, or mismatched state now always redirects reason=invalid_state and clears the state cookie, regardless of whether the callback also carried a providerError.
decisions.reason: The prior ordering checked providerError first, so a forged cross-site callback such as ?error=access_denied with no or mismatched state was accepted as a 'clean' denial - consuming the victim's state cookie (cleared unconditionally at the top of the handler) without ever proving the callback belonged to the browser that started the attempt, letting an attacker invalidate a victim's active OAuth attempt. Google's web-server OAuth flow requires the returned state to match the request state on both consent and denial. apps/api/test/oauth-flow.e2e-spec.ts updated: the missing-state and mismatched-state provider-error cases now expect invalid_state (previously incorrectly expected access_denied, which is what fix-request-review-015 #1 flagged as institutionalizing the defect); a valid-matching-state provider denial still expects access_denied with no session; a new regression test proves a forged no-cookie error=access_denied callback is rejected as invalid_state, sets no session, and does not disturb a separate legitimate in-flight attempt's own cookie/state pair. Backend unit 310/310 and e2e 140/140 re-run clean against the shared local-dev stack (ai/tasks/MEMORIES-0005/evidence/backend-e2e.log).

decisions.decision: review-cycle-16 #1: OAuthController.callback (libs/modules/identity-access/src/presentation/http/oauth.controller.ts) no longer reads-and-clears the state cookie unconditionally at the top of the handler. It now parses the provider first (unsupported -> redirect, cookie untouched), then reads the cookie and requires an exact `state === cookieState` match; only once that match is proven does it call res.clearCookie (exactly once, immediately before branching to access_denied/success). Any unsupported-provider, missing-state, or mismatched-state callback now leaves whatever state cookie is present on the response entirely alone.
decisions.reason: fix-request-review-016 #1: the state cookie is SameSite=Lax (required, since the provider's redirect back is a top-level GET from accounts.google.com), so it is still attached to a forged top-level-GET callback the attacker tricks the victim's browser into making — even one with a missing/mismatched state or an unsupported provider param. The prior code cleared the cookie unconditionally before validating any of that, so a forged request could delete a different, still-valid in-flight OAuth attempt's cookie out from under it, making the victim's genuine callback fail right after with invalid_state (a real, if narrow, denial-of-service on the victim's own login attempt). apps/api/test/oauth-flow.e2e-spec.ts: replaced the old single-request 'forged callback' regression test (which reused a manually-copied cookie string across independent supertest requests and could never actually prove browser cookie-jar behavior either way) with 'rejects forged and unsupported-provider callbacks on the same browser session ...', built on a real `request.agent(...)` cookie jar so Set-Cookie effects from earlier requests genuinely propagate to later ones exactly like a browser tab. Discovered along the way: `supertest`'s server-object request form always issues requests to the literal 127.0.0.1, which never matches this app's Domain=localhost state cookie under a real cookie-jar client (cookiejar does correct domain matching, unlike `.set('Cookie', ...)` header injection) — the new test instead builds the agent against an explicit `http://localhost:<port>` base URL once the app is listening, which does match; see the new knowledge_updates entry. The new test proves: (a) a state-mismatched forged callback and (b) an unsupported-provider (twitter) callback on the same session both leave a separate, real in-flight Google state cookie intact, so the legitimate callback with that state still succeeds afterward; and (c) replaying that same now-consumed callback URL afterward correctly fails invalid_state, proving the cookie really was cleared exactly once, on the legitimate callback. Backend unit 310/310, e2e 142/142 (was 140/140 — net +2: this replacement test plus the new provider_unavailable test from #2 below) all re-run clean (ai/tasks/MEMORIES-0005/evidence/backend-e2e.log).

decisions.decision: Attempt 56 (review cycle 17, fix-request-review-017.md, 2 major findings, full-plan scope): #1 fixed — GoogleOAuthClient now implements a full OIDC ID-token verification flow instead of relying on the userinfo endpoint alone. `start` mints an independent, unpredictable `nonce` alongside `state` (both randomBytes(24).base64url) and stores both in the one state cookie as `${state}.${nonce}` (oauth-state.helper.ts's encodeOAuthStateCookieValue/readOAuthStateCookie now round-trip a {state, nonce} pair — base64url's alphabet never contains '.', so this needs no second cookie or config/env schema change). `buildAuthorizationUrl`/`exchangeCodeForProfile` on the shared `OAuthClient` port both gained a `nonce` parameter; `OAuthLoginInput` gained a `nonce` field forwarded unchanged from the cookie through `OAuthLoginUseCase` to the client. `GoogleOAuthClient.exchangeCodeForProfile` now requests `id_token` (already returned because `scope=openid`) and verifies it end to end in a new `verifyIdToken`: well-formed JWT, RS256 signature checked against Google's live JWKS (https://www.googleapis.com/oauth2/v3/certs, in-memory cached for 1h) using Node's built-in `crypto.createPublicKey({format:'jwk'})` + `crypto.verify` (no new dependency — `jose`/`jwks-rsa` were considered and rejected since Node 20's built-in crypto already covers JWK-format RSA verification), trusted issuer (`accounts.google.com`/`https://accounts.google.com`), audience === configured client id, not expired, and — the actual state/nonce security requirement — `nonce` claim exactly matching the value this exchange's authorization request embedded. Any failure throws before the userinfo call or any OAuthLoginUseCase persistence is ever reached. `FacebookOAuthClient` (deferred/unreachable code) also gained the `nonce` parameter to satisfy the shared interface but ignores it (`void _nonce`) — plain OAuth has no ID-token/nonce concept. #2 fixed — `OAuthController.callback` now allowlists provider errors: only the standard OAuth2 `access_denied` value is reported as user cancellation; every other value (server_error, temporarily_unavailable, invalid_request, or anything unrecognized) maps to a stable, safe `provider_error` reason instead — never echoing the provider's raw error string to the client. `oauth-redirect-handler.tsx` gained a `provider_error` message mapping and was also tightened to only ever act on the literal `success`/`error` `oauth` query values — a garbage/unrecognized value (e.g. a bare `?oauth=whatever` forged link) is now ignored outright instead of being treated as an implicit success whenever a real session happens to already be authenticated (missing-validation-evidence item 3).
decisions.reason: fix-request-review-017.md: #1 — the authorization URL only ever carried client_id/redirect_uri/response_type/scope/state; OAuthController stored only the state cookie, and the token/profile flow validated neither an ID-token nonce nor any equivalent one-time binding, so task.md §11's explicit 'kiểm tra state/nonce' requirement was only half-implemented (state only) and completely untested for nonce. #2 — every nonempty provider error was redirected as reason=access_denied ('Bạn đã hủy đăng nhập.'), so a genuine provider-side fault (server_error/temporarily_unavailable/invalid_request) was misreported to the user as their own cancellation, failing AC3's 'thông báo có thể hiểu được' for callback errors specifically.

knowledge_updates.summary: Google and Facebook OAuth are both implemented end to end at the provider-client/use-case level (authorization-code flow, profile exchange, account linking by (provider, providerSubject)) but as of 2026-08-18 BOTH are deliberately deferred/disabled on the PUBLIC portal's public HTTP surface — OAuthController fails every provider closed before contacting OAuthClientRegistry, regardless of env config. Only LOCAL phone/password is live on the public surface today. Link/create rule: an AuthIdentity resolves an Account strictly by (provider, providerSubject) — provider-supplied email is never used to cross-link to an existing LOCAL or other-provider Account. Apple remains contract-only/unimplemented.
knowledge_updates.content:
## Trạng thái hiện tại (2026-08-18)

Google và Facebook OAuth đã được cài đặt đầy đủ ở tầng provider-client/use-case (authorization-code flow, verify ID token OIDC, exchange profile, gắn `Account` theo `(provider, providerSubject)` — email do provider cung cấp không bao giờ dùng để cross-link sang `Account` LOCAL hoặc provider khác) nhưng **cả hai đều đang bị vô hiệu hóa** trên public surface của `identity-access`: `OAuthController.parseSocialProvider` reject mọi provider trước khi chạm `OAuthClientRegistry`, nên `/auth/oauth/:provider/start|callback` fail closed bất kể cấu hình env. Google bị hoãn vì đang chờ thông tin OAuth client id/secret thật từ Google (chưa có credential production); Facebook bị hoãn vì provider contract chưa được xác minh độc lập. Mã của cả hai được giữ lại làm deferred code (đăng ký DI nhưng không nằm trong `OAUTH_CLIENTS` đang hoạt động) để bật lại khi có đủ thông tin. Apple vẫn chỉ ở mức contract, chưa triển khai.

knowledge_updates.summary: TypeOrmUnitOfWork.withTransaction is now reentrant: if called while a transaction is already active on the current async context (TypeOrmQueryRunnerContext), it joins that transaction (just runs the callback) instead of opening a second, independent connection/transaction. This lets a use case that calls another transactional use case (e.g. RegisterUseCase wrapping CreateAccountUseCase) get one atomic operation for free by wrapping the whole flow in its own outer withTransaction — the inner use case's own withTransaction call needs no change. Every repository already resolves its query runner through the same TypeOrmQueryRunnerContext, so this composes transparently across module boundaries.

## TypeOrmUnitOfWork reentrant

`TypeOrmUnitOfWork.withTransaction` giờ reentrant: nếu gọi trong lúc đã có transaction đang mở trên async context hiện tại (`TypeOrmQueryRunnerContext`), nó join transaction đó (chỉ chạy callback) thay vì mở connection/transaction thứ hai. Nhờ vậy một use case gọi use case khác cũng transactional (ví dụ `RegisterUseCase` bọc `CreateAccountUseCase`) tự động có 1 transaction atomic chung chỉ bằng cách bọc toàn bộ flow trong `withTransaction` ở ngoài cùng — use case bên trong không cần đổi gì. Mọi repository đều resolve query runner qua cùng `TypeOrmQueryRunnerContext` nên cơ chế này compose xuyên module boundary.

knowledge_updates.summary: e2e testing gotcha: this backend's cookies (e.g. the OAuth state cookie, the refresh cookie) are issued with an explicit `Domain` attribute (AUTH_REFRESH_COOKIE_DOMAIN, 'localhost' in every local/test env). `supertest`'s server-object request form (`request(app.getHttpServer())`) always issues requests against the literal `127.0.0.1`, regardless of what address the server actually listens on — so a real `request.agent(...)` cookie jar (which does correct domain matching, unlike the common `.set('Cookie', ...)` header-injection pattern used throughout this suite) will silently never resend a `Domain=localhost` cookie back to a `127.0.0.1` request. A cookie-jar-based e2e test that needs real Set-Cookie/domain semantics (e.g. proving one request's response does or doesn't affect a later request's cookie, as opposed to manually forwarding a captured cookie string) must construct the agent against an explicit string base URL — `request.agent(`http://localhost:${port}`)`, with `port` read from the already-listening `httpServer.address()` — not `request.agent(app.getHttpServer())`. See apps/api/test/oauth-flow.e2e-spec.ts's 'rejects forged and unsupported-provider callbacks on the same browser session ...' test (review-cycle-16 #1).

## e2e gotcha: supertest + cookie Domain

Cookie backend phát ra (OAuth state cookie, refresh cookie) có `Domain` tường minh (`AUTH_REFRESH_COOKIE_DOMAIN`, là `localhost` ở mọi env local/test). `supertest`'s server-object form (`request(app.getHttpServer())`) luôn gửi request tới `127.0.0.1` bất kể server thật sự listen ở đâu — nên `request.agent(...)` (cookie jar thật, có domain matching đúng) sẽ không bao giờ tự động resend lại cookie `Domain=localhost` cho request `127.0.0.1`. Test cần cookie-jar/Set-Cookie semantics thật (chứ không chỉ forward tay 1 cookie string) phải tạo agent với base URL tường minh dạng string — `request.agent(\`http://localhost:${port}\`)`, `port` lấy từ `httpServer.address()` sau khi app đã listen — không dùng `request.agent(app.getHttpServer())`.

knowledge_updates.summary: Verifying a third-party OIDC ID token (signature + issuer/audience/expiry/nonce claims) does not require adding a JWT/JWKS dependency to this backend: Node 20's built-in `node:crypto` already covers it end to end — `crypto.createPublicKey({key: jwk, format:'jwk'})` accepts a provider's published JWKS key object directly (no PEM conversion needed), and the one-shot `crypto.verify(algorithm, data, key, signature)` checks an RS256 signature without `jsonwebtoken`/`jose`/`jwks-rsa`. See GoogleOAuthClient.verifyIdToken (libs/modules/identity-access/src/infrastructure/security/google-oauth.client.ts) for the reference implementation: base64url-decode the three JWT segments, match `kid` against a cached JWKS fetch, verify the signature over `${header}.${payload}`, then check `iss`/`aud`/`exp`/`nonce` as plain claim comparisons.

## Verify OIDC ID token bằng node:crypto có sẵn

Verify chữ ký + issuer/audience/expiry/nonce của ID token OIDC bên thứ ba KHÔNG cần thêm dependency JWT/JWKS — `node:crypto` (Node 20+) đã đủ: `crypto.createPublicKey({key: jwk, format: 'jwk'})` nhận thẳng JWK key từ JWKS endpoint của provider (không cần convert PEM), và `crypto.verify(algorithm, data, key, signature)` verify chữ ký RS256 mà không cần `jsonwebtoken`/`jose`/`jwks-rsa`. Xem `GoogleOAuthClient.verifyIdToken` (`libs/modules/identity-access/src/infrastructure/security/google-oauth.client.ts`) làm reference: base64url-decode 3 segment JWT, match `kid` với JWKS đã cache, verify chữ ký trên `${header}.${payload}`, rồi so sánh `iss`/`aud`/`exp`/`nonce`.
